:::{#def-similar}
#### Similar matrices

Two $p \times p$ matrices $\matr{A}$ and $\matr{B}$ are **similar**
if $\matr{B} = \matr{P}^{-1} \matr{A} \matr{P}$
for some invertible $p \times p$ matrix $\matr{P}$ (@def-invertible-matrix).

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-similar-both-ways}
#### Similarity read both ways

If $\matr{P}$ is invertible, then $\matr{P}^{-1}$ is invertible with inverse $\matr{P}$:
$\matr{P}^{-1} \matr{P} = \matr{P} \matr{P}^{-1} = \matr{I}_p$ (@def-matrix-inverse)
is the condition of @def-invertible-matrix for $\matr{P}^{-1}$ with $\matr{P}$ as the other factor,
and that factor is unique (@rem-invertible-inverse).
If $\matr{B} = \matr{P}^{-1} \matr{A} \matr{P}$, then

$$
\ba
\matr{P} \matr{B} \matr{P}^{-1}
&= \matr{P}\,(\matr{P}^{-1} \matr{A} \matr{P})\,\matr{P}^{-1}
&& \text{(substitute } \matr{B} \text{)}
\\
&= (\matr{P} \matr{P}^{-1})\,\matr{A}\,(\matr{P} \matr{P}^{-1})
&& \text{(@thm-matmul-assoc)}
\\
&= \matr{I}_p\,\matr{A}\,\matr{I}_p
&& \text{(@def-matrix-inverse)}
\\
&= \matr{A},
&& \text{(@thm-identity)}
\ea
$$

and the same steps with $\matr{P}$ and $\matr{P}^{-1}$ exchanged turn
$\matr{A} = \matr{P} \matr{B} \matr{P}^{-1}$ back into $\matr{B} = \matr{P}^{-1} \matr{A} \matr{P}$.
So $\matr{B} = \matr{P}^{-1} \matr{A} \matr{P}$ exactly when $\matr{A} = \matr{P} \matr{B} \matr{P}^{-1}$,
and similarity goes both ways:
$\matr{A}$ is similar to $\matr{B}$ through $\matr{P}^{-1}$, whose inverse is $\matr{P}$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-similar}
#### A matrix similar to a diagonal one

Let $\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$
and $\matr{P} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 \end{bmatrix}$.
Then

$$
\ba
\matr{P}^2
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 \cd 1 + 1 \cd 1 & 1 \cd 1 + 1 \cd (-1) \\ 1 \cd 1 + (-1) \cd 1 & 1 \cd 1 + (-1)(-1) \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(@def-matrix-mult)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(arithmetic)}
\\
&= 2\,\matr{I}_2,
&& \text{(@def-scalar-mult, @def-identity-matrix)}
\ea
$$

so $\matr{P}\,(\tfrac{1}{2}\,\matr{P}) = \tfrac{1}{2}\,\matr{P}^2 = \matr{I}_2$
and likewise $(\tfrac{1}{2}\,\matr{P})\,\matr{P} = \matr{I}_2$ (@thm-scalar-matmul):
$\matr{P}^{-1} = \tfrac{1}{2}\,\matr{P}$ (@def-matrix-inverse). Then

$$
\ba
\matr{P}^{-1} \matr{A} \matr{P}
&= (\tfrac{1}{2}\,\matr{P})\,\matr{A} \matr{P}
&& \text{(substitute } \matr{P}^{-1} \text{)}
\\
&= \tfrac{1}{2}\,(\matr{P} \matr{A} \matr{P})
&& \text{(@thm-scalar-matmul)}
\\
&= \tfrac{1}{2}\,\matr{P}\,(\matr{A} \matr{P})
&& \text{(@thm-matmul-assoc)}
\\
&= \tfrac{1}{2} \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 1 \\ 3 & -1 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(@def-matrix-mult, for } \matr{A} \matr{P} \text{)}
\\
&= \tfrac{1}{2} \begin{bmatrix} 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(@def-matrix-mult)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix},
&& \text{(@def-scalar-mult)}
\ea
$$

so $\matr{A}$ is similar to $\diag(3, 1)$.
At the other extreme, the identity matrix is similar only to itself:
$\matr{P}^{-1} \matr{I}_p \matr{P} = \matr{P}^{-1} \matr{P} = \matr{I}_p$ for every invertible $\matr{P}$
(@thm-identity, @def-matrix-inverse).

:::
